title: Audit telemetry residency policy enforcement and immutable evidence exporter
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Goal: Implement end-to-end enforcement of data residency and retention policies at the audit-ingestion and export layers, plus an immutable evidence exporter that produces tamper-evident WORM bundles suitable for regulatory audits. This ticket covers policy enforcement rules, ingestion-time provenance tagging, immutable snapshot creation, notarization metadata (hashes + HSM anchor), and an automated export/reporting workflow for compliance teams.
acceptance_criteria: 1) Audit events are tagged with residency and retention metadata when ingested, based on the request context and account policy. 2) Retention matrix is enforced automatically: expired events are only deleted via a sealed job that produces an auditable tombstone manifest. 3) Immutable exporter can produce a WORM bundle for a given account/region/date range; the bundle includes an index, content hashes, a manifest, and an HSM-anchored timestamp. 4) Exported bundles validate against internal integrity checks and appear in the Compliance Console with an evidence record. 5) Automation runs on a schedule and supports on-demand exports initiated by the Compliance team. 6) Unit and e2e tests cover policy mismatch cases (cross-region writes, emergency override), and CI gates block merges until tests pass.
tasks:
- Design: residency/retention decision matrix and policy schema (PM + Legal input)
- Runtime: ingestion hook to attach provenance metadata and route to region-locked topics
- Storage: implement immutable snapshot writer that writes to WORM-backed buckets and rotates manifests
- Integrity: compute content hashes, generate manifest, and call HSM anchoring service to notarize snapshot hash
- Exporter: HTTP endpoint and scheduled job that packages bundles and notifies Compliance Console with evidence record
- Rollout: canary to internal org, smoke tests, then wider rollout with backout plan
- Docs: runbook for auditors and ops, sample verification script, and FAQ for SRE/Support
notes: Trade-offs discussed: 1) immediate HSM anchoring for each event vs batching per snapshot (we chose snapshot anchoring to control HSM cost and rate limits); 2) strict residency enforcement at ingress vs soft tagging with later enforcement (ingress enforcement chosen to reduce downstream compliance risk). Open questions: exact TTL semantics for locked vs mutable audit categories; legal review on minimum retention granularity. See design doc for details.
rollout_plan: 1) Feature branch and integration tests in CI. 2) Internal canary on dev environment for one week, monitor seal latency and error rate. 3) Small tenant canary with 2 enterprise customers (opt-in). 4) Gradual ramp by region with automatic fallback to archival-only path if exporter errors. 5) Full global rollout after 4 weeks of stable metrics.
metrics:
- ingest_provenance_tag_rate (target 100%)
- snapshot_seal_duration_p50/p95 (target p95 < 30s)
- export_bundle_validation_failures (target 0)
- evidence_delivery_latency (target < 5m)
- cross_region_policy_violations (target 0)
qa_checks:
- Synthetic test that writes cross-region event and verifies rejection or re-route.
- Export validation script that recomputes hashes from bundle and verifies HSM anchor.
- Retention expiry simulation: mark events as expired and ensure tombstone manifest is produced.
- Security review checklist completed and signed off by Security team.
progress_updates: 2026-03-02: Kickoff meeting with PM and Legal; residency matrix draft completed. 2026-03-05: Prototype exporter writes a local manifest and computes hashes; HSM integration POC accepted. 2026-03-09: Ingestion hook implemented for prototype, tagging events in dev. 2026-03-12: Security review scheduled and canary cohort defined.
